CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1 -- data/martindelcampo_2020_juarez_violence.py melts the .sav columns TIPI1..TIPI10 under their own names (no rename, no positional step), so the IRW code IS the source column name. item_text = the .sav VARIABLE label of that column, 10/10, verbatim. option_text = the .sav VALUE labels, identical on all 10 columns (labels29 on TIPI1-2, labels30-37 on TIPI3-10, same seven strings): 1 Disagree strongly .. 7 Agree strongly, kept verbatim including the capital in 'Agree Moderately'; matches the paper's '1 = Strongly Disagree to 7 = Strongly Agree'. Live data reproduce the .sav cell for cell: 2980/2980 id x item cells agree (298 ids x 10 items, no missing), and every item uses all 7 levels. STORED DIRECTION: raw, not reversed -- the five canonical TIPI pairs correlate negatively (1x6 -0.356, 2x7 -0.123, 3x8 -0.251, 4x9 -0.311, 5x10 -0.110), and the .sav's own reverse-coded copies BF2r/BF4r/BF6r/BF8r/BF10r equal 8 minus TIPI2/4/6/8/10 exactly (298/298 each), i.e. the study's reverse set is the canonical even items. WORDING DEVIATES FROM GOSLING'S ENGLISH: the labels follow canonical TIPI order 1-10 but six pairs are not Gosling's wording -- TIPI2 'Critic, fighter' (canonical 'Critical, quarrelsome'), TIPI3 'Reliable, self-disciplined' ('Dependable, self-disciplined'), TIPI4 'Anxious, easy to alter' ('Anxious, easily upset'), TIPI7 'Nice, warm' ('Sympathetic, warm'), TIPI8 'Disorganized, carefree' ('Disorganized, careless'), TIPI9 'Quiet, emotionally stable' ('Calm, emotionally stable'). These read as English renderings of a Spanish form (e.g. 'fácil de alterar', 'tranquilo'); shipped as the study wrote them, NOT normalised to canonical wording. LANGUAGE FALLBACK: respondents were Mexican undergraduates at UACJ, the other instruments are cited as Mexican/Spanish validations, and the paper cites a Spanish TIPI translation (Romero et al., 2012) while noting the TIPI 'is yet to be validated with a Mexican population'; the paper does not name which Spanish form was used. Spanish wording is not recoverable from the deposit or the paper: .sav variable+value labels have 0 non-ASCII characters and no Spanish text; s002-s004 are AMOS .amw model files; s005.xlsx has no TIPI text and 0 non-ASCII strings; the PeerJ text gives only the English example 'extraverted/enthusiastic'. So the study's own English labels ship in the base fields with language=Spanish and empty _translated columns (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied). instructions blank: no administered TIPI instruction or stem is published in the deposit or paper (Gosling's 'I see myself as:' preamble deliberately not imported). instrument name is IRW's. Step 3b: 10 items, 1-7 agreement, trait-pair content in canonical TIPI order -- matches the TIPI. RIGHTS: originator Gosling's TIPI page: 'WANT TO USE THE TIPI? GO AHEAD. ANYONE CAN USE IT FOR ANY PURPOSE. NO NEED TO ASK ME FOR PERMISSION.' On translations the same page says 'As far as I know, you are free to use these translations but as a courtesy I encourage you to contact the contact persons listed below before doing so.' -- a courtesy request, not a reserved right (no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution term).
